title: 1954 AHSME Problem 48
statement: A train, an hour after starting, meets with an accident which detains it a half hour, after which it proceeds at \(\dfrac34\) of its former rate and arrives \(3\dfrac12\) hours late. Had the accident happened \(90\) miles farther along the line, it would have arrived only \(3\) hours late. The length of the trip in miles was:

solutions.text:
Let the normal speed be \(v\) and the trip length be \(L.\) Traveling a distance at \(\frac{3v}{4}\) rather than \(v\) adds one-third of its normal travel time. In the first case, \[ \frac12+\frac13\left(\frac Lv-1\right)=\frac72, \] so \(\frac{L}{v}=10.\) If the accident happens \(90\) miles farther along, \[ \frac12+\frac13\left(\frac Lv-1-\frac{90}{v}\right)=3. \] Substituting \(\frac{L}{v}=10\) gives \(\frac{90}{v}=\frac{3}{2},\) hence \(v=60\) and \[ L=10v=600. \]

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let the normal speed be \(v\) and the trip length be \(L\); slowing to \(\frac{3v}{4}\) adds one-third of the normal time on the affected distance
Use the two late-arrival equations to find first \(\frac{L}{v}\), then \(\frac{90}{v}\)
